Story & Plot

In this live-action remake, teenage Moana answers the call of the ocean and ventures beyond the reef of her island home of Motunui. Destined to take over her island, she teams up with the infamous exiled demigod Maui on an unforgettable journey. Together, they embark on a mission to restore prosperity and save their people.

Comedy & Entertainment

The film blends family fantasy and adventure elements into its narrative framework. While carrying a familiar premise, it relies on the dynamic between its main characters to drive the entertainment value. Reviewers note the quick turnaround for a live-action remake of this scale.

Performances & Direction

The cast features Catherine Lagaʻaia as Moana, alongside Dwayne Johnson reprising his role as the demigod Maui. The ensemble also includes Rena Owen as wise grandmother Tala, as well as John Tui and Frankie Adams as Moana's parents, Chief Tui and Sina.

  • Familiar adventure elements
  • Committed cast performances
  • Reprise of key roles
  • Family-friendly adventure

Weaknesses

Reviewers note that the film is a dull and unimpressive remake that features the exact same plot as its predecessor with nothing changing. It struggles to justify its own existence and feels like a fast cash grab in terms of the short amount of time that has elapsed since the original.

Final verdict

Moana (2026) offers little that is new for audiences already familiar with the story, playing out as a very similar live-action experience. Viewers seeking fresh storytelling may want to skip this fast remake, though it retains the core adventure of the original premise.

As a horror and thriller film centered on a haunted hostel and terrifying ghostly encounters, the movie focuses primarily on delivering suspenseful and spooky moments rather than traditional comedic relief.
